ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (neuromuscular) Referral — Dorothea Lange — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Primary care visit for new fatigue, weakness, muscle pain, and falls 55 years after childhood polio; recent heartburn

text.paragraph: New fatigue, slowly increasing weakness in the left leg and both arms as well as the right leg weakened by paralytic polio at seven, muscle aching after work, and two falls, over about 18 months, in a photographer of 61. Is this post-polio syndrome, and how should she be managed so that she can keep working? [S]

list.item: Does she meet the criteria for post-polio syndrome, and have other causes of new weakness been excluded?
How should exercise be prescribed so that it helps without overusing weakened muscles?
Which orthosis and walking aid would prevent falls and still let her work in the field?
Does she need respiratory or sleep studies?
What precautions should be recorded for sedation and anesthesia, since she may need an endoscopy?
How should she pace her work, and what can she expect over the coming years?

text.paragraph: Polio at seven left a weak right leg and a limp; she recovered enough to walk without an aid and has worked for decades, often standing for hours with heavy cameras. For about 18 months she has tired after two hours of activity and noticed weakness in the left leg and both shoulders, with aching in the thighs and shoulders after field days, a cold right foot, and two falls from catching the right foot, without injury. No numbness, swallowing trouble, or breathlessness; sleep is unrefreshing. On examination the right leg is thin with foot drop and knee hyperextension; Timed Up and Go 14 seconds. Same-day blood tests are sent (blood count, chemistry, glucose and HbA1c, TSH, B12, vitamin D, calcium, creatine kinase, ESR, and CRP), and nerve conduction studies and needle EMG are booked; PHQ-9 6. An operation for stomach ulcers in her early fifties, so no NSAIDs. Heartburn for three months, starting an omeprazole trial; endoscopy may be needed. No known allergy. She wants to keep photographing in the field [S]

list.item: New tiredness and weakness, now in the good leg and the arms as well as the leg weakened by polio in childhood, with aching after work and two falls. [S]
Heartburn after meals and at night for three months. [S]
Wants to keep photographing in the field and fears having to give it up. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Dorothea Lange was born Dorothea Margaretta Nutzhorn in Hoboken, New Jersey, on May 26, 1895. [D]
At the age of seven, in 1902, Lange had polio, which left her with a weakened right leg and a lifelong limp. [D]

Lange was a documentary photographer. In 1935 she was hired as a photographer for the Resettlement Administration, later the Farm Security Administration, and in March 1936 she made the photograph known as "Migrant Mother" in Nipomo, California. From the mid-1930s she lived in Berkeley, California. [D]
In the late 1940s ill health stopped Lange working: she had a succession of severe stomach ulcers that were controlled only by radical surgery, and pain and discomfort troubled her from then on. [D]
In the early 1950s Lange returned to work with photographic essays for Life and Fortune and helped to found the photography magazine Aperture; her poor health limited her to short bursts of work. [D]

Work-up of new weakness as a diagnosis of exclusion: blood count, chemistry, glucose and HbA1c, TSH, B12, vitamin D, calcium, creatine kinase, ESR and CRP today; nerve conduction studies and needle EMG; PHQ-9; sleep screen. Guideline: EFNS guideline on diagnosis and management of post-polio syndrome. Report of an EFNS task force. Eur J Neurol 2006;13(8):795-801 (2006); Post-Polio Syndrome: Identifying Best Practices in Diagnosis & Care (diagnostic criteria for post-polio syndrome) (2001) [S]

Heartburn: lifestyle measures and an eight-week trial of omeprazole 20 mg before breakfast; endoscopy if alarm features appear or if symptoms return when it is stopped. Guideline: ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease. Am J Gastroenterol 2022;117(1):27-56 (2022) [S]

Fall prevention: home hazard review, footwear, night lighting, rails on the garden path, and a bone density scan for a woman with a weakened limb and falls. Guideline: World guidelines for falls prevention and management for older adults: a global initiative. Age Ageing 2022;51(9):afac205 (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, osteoporosis monograph (2026) [S]

Pain care: acetaminophen as needed, heat, pacing, and stretching; no nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs after her ulcer surgery. Guideline: EFNS guideline on diagnosis and management of post-polio syndrome. Report of an EFNS task force. Eur J Neurol 2006;13(8):795-801 (2006) [S]
